subject: Ricoh: SLO qualification & proposed SLA language (latency measurement + exclusions)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@ricoh.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & follow-ups from today — latency/throughput targets

Hi Susan — thanks again for making time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and next steps: 

- Target latency: Ricoh product team expects 95th-percentile rounding of "end-to-end" response time under 200ms for non-streamed text generation at 256 token requests. Streaming endpoints need token-flush latency under 50ms for first byte.
- Throughput/concurrency: production peak estimated at ~500 concurrent requests across three regions, with bursts up to ~1.5k sustained for ~10-15 minutes.
- Workload mix: ~70% short prompts (<128 tokens), 25% medium (128-512), 5% long.
- Security: Ricoh will require Private deployment for PII workloads; hosted API ok for analytics.

Can you confirm the latency targets above map to what you shared on the call? I attached a first-pass SLO/SLA wording (Ricoh-SLO-draft-v1.docx) that translates these targets into measurement definitions and remedies — Ben and I would appreciate any edits.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm measurement points (client-side e2e vs service ingress-to-egress) by EOD Wed (08/05).
2) We iterate SLA language and produce a doc for legal by 08/10.
3) Technical deep-dive with your infra team (Alex) — propose Wed 08/12.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@ricoh.com>

Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@ricoh.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & follow-ups from today — latency/throughput targets

Thanks Karthik — that summary is accurate and helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- When we said 200ms we were referring to client-observed end-to-end, measured from the moment our service issues the request to Redwood until the final token is received by our service. For streaming use-cases we care about first-byte latency for interactive agents (desktop app).
- For SLOs we typically define obligations at p95 and p99 depending on the contract tier; for our initial pilot we want a p95 target of 200ms and a p99 that is "reasonable" but with clear exclusions for scheduled maintenance and regional outages.
- Concurrency: the 500 concurrent estimate is per-region, so global could be higher. We will confirm exact numbers but plan shows 3 US regions + EU staging.

One ask: can you include a proposed reporting cadence and sample dashboard that shows p95/p99, errors, and per-route token breakdown? That will help our procurement team evaluate.

Regards,
Susan Lee

Ricoh Enterprise

Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft SLA language + measurement diagram attached

Susan — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is a slightly updated draft that: 

- Defines latency measurement as ingress-to-egress at the Redwood gateway (server-side) and shows an optional client-observed clause. We note both in the SLA and allow Ricoh to choose which is the primary metric for remedies.
- Proposes p95 = 200ms (non-stream), p50-first-byte for streaming and first-byte <=50ms target; p99 set as a "best-effort" threshold with reporting but limited remedies unless p99 degradation is sustained across 24h windows.
- Adds explicit exclusions: scheduled maintenance (windowed), force majeure, DDoS when mitigation in progress, and customer-side network issues (with a short diagnostic trace requirement).
- Reporting: weekly automated dashboard (retention 90 days) and monthly executive summary. Incident reports for SLA violations within 24 hours.

I've attached a small diagram (latency-measurement-diagram.png) that shows where we instrument for ingress/egress measurement vs client-side timing. Please review and call out any redlines. Ben — can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the weekly dashboard sample and a short retention/aggregation note for the procurement packet?

Thanks,
Karthik

Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Draft SLA language + measurement diagram attached

Looping in a couple of suggestions from legal and the product SLO team — quick bullets so we don't lose momentum: 

- Remedies: instead of immediate credits at p99 blips, propose a tiered approach: (a) p95 breaches trigger credit schedule A; (b) sustained p99 breaches over a rolling 24h window escalate to credit schedule B + root cause analysis; (c) catastrophic regional failures follow emergency response playbook. This aligns incentives and avoids noisy credits for transient network noise.
- Measurement windows: define rolling-window aggregation (5 minute buckets) and require at least 95% sample coverage for a valid measurement window.
- Exclusions: add a clause for customer-driven configuration changes (e.g., enabling very large context windows mid-flight) — we'll require a 48h notice for major workload-shape changes that materially affect latency.

Susan / Alex — if those are acceptable we'll incorporate legal wording into the SLO doc and return a near-final for your procurement by 08/10. Karthik/Ben — can you prepare the dashboard sample and send a short note on how we classify streaming vs non-streaming endpoints (tokenization, first-byte flush definition)?

Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
